flashcard_questions.q: Which island dispute of 1921 did the League settle between Sweden and Finland?
Which country was awarded those islands by the League?
How did the League settle the 1921 dispute over Upper Silesia?
flashcard_questions.a: It held a plebiscite and split the region by the vote.

flashcard_questions.q: Which country invaded Bulgaria in 1925 before the League ordered a withdrawal?
What did the losing side complain of after the League acted firmly in 1925?
flashcard_questions.a: Double standards, because Italy had not been stopped over Corfu.

flashcard_questions.q: How many prisoners of war did the League's Refugee Commission return home?
Which League body led global campaigns against malaria and leprosy?
Which substance did the International Labour Organisation succeed in banning from paint?
How many slaves did the League's Slavery Commission free in Sierra Leone?
Which city, Lithuania's historic capital, did Poland seize by force in 1920?
Why did the League fail to act over Poland's seizure of that city?
flashcard_questions.a: France saw Poland as a key ally and would not act.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Greek island did Mussolini bombard and occupy in 1923?
In which year did the murder of an Italian general trigger that occupation?
Which body took the dispute away from the League and sided with Italy?

notes: 14 cards: 5 dispute-to-outcome, 4 humanitarian body to achievement, 3 place, 2 cause-effect. Lean lesson, so 14; the Health Organisation card names the body rather than listing both diseases as an answer.
